title: Real Madrid sanctioned by UEFA after fan performed Nazi salute before Champions League tie
content:
Real Madrid have been given a suspended partial stadium closure order and fined €15,000 (£13,021; $17,371) after a supporter was found to have performed a Nazi salute before a Champions League match by UEFA.

The incident took place in the Grada Fans section, located in the south side of the Bernabeu, before Madrid’s 2-1 Champions League play-off win over Benfica on February 25.

The incident was investigated by European football’s governing body’s Control, Ethics and Disciplinary Body. It confirmed in a statement on Friday it had ordered the closure of a section in the lower south stand in the Bernabeu, consisting of 500 seats, for one game “for the racist and/or discriminatory behaviour of its supporters.”

The ban only applies to UEFA competitions and is suspended for a year, meaning that the area of the stadium will remain open for Madrid’s Champions League last-16 first leg against Manchester City on Wednesday.

The fan in question was identified by security staff during February’s fixture and ejected from the stadium after footage emerged of him appearing to make the gesture before kick-off.

Madrid confirmed that they had opened disciplinary proceedings following the game, stating that the club “condemns these types of gestures and expressions that incite violence and hatred in sport and in society.”

The Athletic has approached Madrid for comment.

Performing a Nazi salute is not a criminal offence in Spain, unlike in other European countries such as Germany and Italy, though it can be punishable by law if the gesture is accompanied by other acts which constitute a hate crime.

Before the Champions League tie against Benfica, a large “no to racism” banner was unveiled by Madrid fans as the teams lined up and the competition’s anthem played. The banner was displayed in the wake of Madrid forward Vinicius Junior accusing Benfica’s Gianluca Prestianni of racially abusing him during the first leg. Prestianni denies the allegations, and served a one-game provisional suspension for the second leg while UEFA investigates. UEFA said he had been suspended “without prejudice”.
